facts.statement: Kileskus is a genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaur named after the Khakas word for "lizard" and was discovered in the Itat Formation of Russia.
facts.quote: Kileskus (meaning "lizard" in the Khakas language) is a genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaur known from partial remains found in Middle Jurassic (Bathonian stage) Itat Formation of Sharypovsky District, Krasnoyarsk Krai (Russia).

facts.statement: The type species Kileskus aristotocus was named in 2010 by Averianov and colleagues.
facts.quote: The type species is K. aristotocus, named in 2010 by Averianov and colleagues.

facts.statement: Known fossils include a maxilla, premaxilla, surangular, and some hand and foot bones.
facts.quote: Fossils recovered include the holotype maxilla, a premaxilla, a surangular, and a few bones from the hand and foot.

facts.statement: The skull bones of Kileskus are similar to those of Proceratosaurus.
facts.quote: The skull bones are similar to those of Proceratosaurus.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses have classified Kileskus as a basal proceratosaurid.
facts.quote: Kileskus has been included in two phylogenetic analyses and found to be a basal proceratosaurid both times.

facts.statement: It is unknown whether Kileskus had a nasal crest, but it is assigned to Proceratosauridae based on other features.
facts.quote: Although it is unknown whether Kileskus sported a nasal crest, it can be assigned to Proceratosauridae due to a number of other features.

facts.statement: Kileskus shares with Proceratosaurus nares inclined at a 40-degree angle to the skull.
facts.quote: Kileskus also shares with Proceratosaurus nares inclined posterodorsally at a 40-degree angle to the skull.

facts.statement: Kileskus is distinguished from other proceratosaurids by its maxilla's anterior rim being confluent with the ascending process and gently sloping posterodorsally.
facts.quote: Kileskus is distinguished from other proceratosaurids by the anterior rim of its maxilla being confluent with the ascending process of the maxilla and gently sloping posterodorsally.

facts.statement: Kileskus lived approximately 166 million years ago in the Middle Jurassic, about 100 million years before Tyrannosaurus emerged.
facts.quote: Kileskus, one of the geologically oldest known tyrannosauroids, lived in the Middle Jurassic (~166 million years ago), 100 million years before the emergence of Tyrannosaurus, providing critical early-stage physical evidence for how tyrannosauroids first evolved.

facts.statement: Kileskus is considered an important discovery in 21st-century paleontology for understanding tyrannosauroid evolution.
facts.quote: Kileskus is arguably an important discovery of the 21st-century palaeontology.

facts.statement: Kileskus lived in the Middle Jurassic, approximately 167 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 167 millones de años, en el Bathoniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Kileskus is the Bathonian stage, from 168.2 to 165.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Bathonian (168.2 to 165.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Additional remains attributed to the genus include cervical and caudal vertebrae and a fibula.
rejected.quote: Additional remains referred to the genus include cervical and caudal vertebrae, as well as a fibula.
